primitives.name: PUSH
primitives.description: Push `A` from `D` onto `S`.

primitives.name: POP
primitives.description: Remove the top value `A` from `S` and push it onto `D`.

primitives.name: TOP
primitives.description: Copy the top value `A` from `S` onto `D`.

primitives.name: SNAPSHOT
primitives.description: Copy the contents of `S` as a list onto `D`.

primitives.name: DEPTH
primitives.description: Count the values on `S` and push the count onto `D`. The count is also 0 for a word that has no stack (`EXISTS` tells it apart from an empty one) and for a primitive, whose stack holds no values.

primitives.name: EXISTS
primitives.description: Report whether `S` exists, without creating it.

primitives.name: LOCKED
primitives.description: Report whether `S` is locked, as every primitive's stack is and `LOCK` makes any other: it then refuses `PUSH`, `POP`, `DELETE` and the like. The default stack is not locked, and the result is also 0 for a word that has no stack (`EXISTS` reports 0 for it).

primitives.name: LEXICON
primitives.description: On `S`, push the list `L` of the selectors of every word that has a stack, that is, every one for which `EXISTS` reports 1, primitives and emptied stacks included, ordered by name. Each selector is a unit containing the word, so it can be used as it is. Filter the list in Bo and map `CLEAR` or `DELETE` over what is left.

primitives.name: CLEAR
primitives.description: On `S`, remove all values.

primitives.name: DELETE
primitives.description: On `S`, remove the stack itself, so that `EXISTS` reports 0 for it and its values are lost; pushing to it again creates it anew. The default stack and locked stacks, which include every primitive, cannot be deleted (`Permission-Error`); deleting an unlocked primitive's stack only discards its definitions, and the primitive remains. `CLEAR` only empties a stack, which then continues to exist.

primitives.name: LOCK
primitives.description: On `S`, protect against mutation: it then refuses `PUSH`, `POP`, `CLEAR`, `DELETE` and the like. Locking a locked stack changes nothing. The default stack cannot be locked (`Permission-Error`).

primitives.name: UNLOCK
primitives.description: On `S`, remove mutation protection. Unlocking a stack that is not locked, such as the default stack, changes nothing. Unlocking a primitive's stack lets a definition shadow the primitive.

primitives.name: DROP
primitives.description: On `S`, remove the top value.

primitives.name: PICK
primitives.description: On `S`, copy the zero-based nth value to the top.

primitives.name: ROLL
primitives.description: On `S`, move the zero-based nth value to the top.

primitives.name: UNIT
primitives.description: On `S`, wrap the top value in a one-element list.

primitives.name: CONSL
primitives.description: On `S`, prepend the element of unit `U` to list `L`.

primitives.name: CONSR
primitives.description: On `S`, append the element of unit `U` to list `L`.

primitives.name: UNCONSL
primitives.description: On `S`, remove the first element of a non-empty list into a unit.

primitives.name: UNCONSR
primitives.description: On `S`, remove the last element of a non-empty list into a unit.

primitives.name: TYPE
primitives.description: On `S`, return 0 for a number, 1 for a list, or 2 for a word.

primitives.name: RATIO
primitives.description: On `S`, return the exact numerator and denominator of number `X`.

primitives.name: APPLY
primitives.description: On `S`, execute the elements of list `L` in order.

primitives.name: IFTE
primitives.description: On `S`, execute `I`, then execute `T` if its result is positive or `E` otherwise.

primitives.name: LOOP
primitives.description: Take `C` and `B` from `S` and repeat: execute `C`, and if its result is positive execute `B` and start again, otherwise stop. The programs run like those of `IFTE`, and the loop leaves no frame that `REC` could find, so a `rec` inside `B` belongs to the enclosing `LAMBDA`. A loop runs in constant control-stack space.

primitives.name: LAMBDA
primitives.description: Run the program `P` in a frame labelled by `s`. The selector is a *virtual* stack selector, a unit containing a word or `()`: it works as a label that is only compared, and no stack is ever created or touched. Inside `P`, `REC` with the same selector runs `P` again. The frame is dropped when `P` ends or an error unwinds it.

primitives.name: REC
primitives.description: Run again the program of the innermost running `LAMBDA` whose label is `s`, as a tail call when nothing follows. The selector is a *virtual* stack selector, like that of `LAMBDA`: a label that creates no stack. Without such a frame `REC` raises `Existence-Error`. Recursive file-local words lower to a labelled `LAMBDA`, so a callback of another recursive word never reaches the wrong frame; `()` is the anonymous label of `lambda` and `rec`.

primitives.name: PARALLEL
primitives.description: On `S`, run quotation `Q` for each item of `L` in isolated workers and collect their final stacks in input order.

primitives.name: ADD
primitives.description: On `S`, add `A` and `B`.

primitives.name: SUB
primitives.description: On `S`, subtract `B` from `A`.

primitives.name: MUL
primitives.description: On `S`, multiply `A` and `B`.

primitives.name: DIV
primitives.description: On `S`, divide `A` by `B` using true division.

primitives.name: IDIV
primitives.description: On `S`, floor-divide `A` by `B`.

primitives.name: POW
primitives.description: On `S`, raise `A` to the power `B`.

primitives.name: RANGE
primitives.description: On `S`, generate an inclusive numeric range from `START` to `END` using `STEP`.

primitives.name: BROADCAST
primitives.description: On `S`, apply the binary operation word held by unit `U` to every pair of elements of numbers or arrays `A` and `B`, aligning shapes from the right. The word runs with the pair on top and must leave exactly one number.

primitives.name: ARRAY
primitives.description: On `S`, validate flat numeric data `F` and shape `Q` and construct array `T`.

primitives.name: SHAPE
primitives.description: On `S`, return the shape list of array `T`.

primitives.name: RANK
primitives.description: On `S`, return the rank of array `T`.

primitives.name: RESHAPE
primitives.description: On `S`, return `T` with shape `Q`; the element count must not change.

primitives.name: FETCH
primitives.description: On `S`, return the zero-based element at index list `I` of array `T`.

primitives.name: STORE
primitives.description: On `S`, return `T` with `x` at zero-based index `I`; `T` remains unchanged.

primitives.name: CHUNK
primitives.description: On `S`, split rank-one array `T` into `n` ordered rank-one array chunks.

primitives.name: CONCAT
primitives.description: On `S`, concatenate an ordered list of rank-one array chunks.

primitives.name: REDUCE
primitives.description: On `S`, fold array `T` over all axes or along one zero-based axis with the binary word held by unit `U`, from left to right starting at each slice's first element. Each step runs `U` with the accumulator and the next element on top; it must leave exactly one number. An empty slice raises `Domain-Error`.

primitives.name: DOT
primitives.description: On `S`, return the dot product of rank-one arrays `A` and `B`.

primitives.name: MEAN
primitives.description: On `S`, compute the arithmetic mean globally or along one axis.

primitives.name: MEDIAN
primitives.description: On `S`, compute the median globally or along one axis.

primitives.name: TRANSPOSE
primitives.description: On `S`, transpose rank-two array `T`.

primitives.name: OUTER
primitives.description: On `S`, return the rank-two outer product of rank-one arrays `A` and `B`.

primitives.name: MATMUL
primitives.description: On `S`, multiply rank-two arrays `A` and `B`.

primitives.name: EQUAL
primitives.description: On `S`, compare values structurally.

primitives.name: OPEN
primitives.description: On `S`, open file `P` with mode `M` and return its handle `H`.

primitives.name: CLOSE
primitives.description: On `S`, close stream `H`.

primitives.name: READ
primitives.description: On `S`, read the next character code from stream `H`, or return -1 at end of file.

primitives.name: WRITE
primitives.description: On `S`, write character code `c` to stream `H`.

primitives.name: INCLUDE
primitives.description: On `S`, lower and execute the source file named by `P`, even if it was already loaded, after taking out what its earlier load left (its private words, the items it pushed, its locks and the stacks it made; see the language guide). The default-stack word `require` skips files that were loaded.

primitives.name: INCLUDED
primitives.description: On `S`, report whether source file `P` has already been loaded; 0 if its load ended in an error.

primitives.name: PARSE
primitives.description: On `S`, read source text `T` and leave the program it denotes as the list `P`, without running it. Invalid source raises `Syntax-Error` with the message and the line within `T`.

primitives.name: CATCH
primitives.description: On `S`, run `T` and, on error, run `H` with the error on top; without an error `H` is not run.

primitives.name: CALL
primitives.description: On `S`, run `SETUP` and `BODY`, then `CLEANUP`; after a body error, run `CATCHER` after cleanup.

primitives.name: THROW
primitives.description: On `S`, raise an error whose kind is the word unit `K` (such as `(Type-Error)`) with data list `L`; any other `K` raises `Type-Error`.

primitives.name: RETHROW
primitives.description: On `S`, propagate existing error `E` without recording it again.

primitives.name: EXIT
primitives.description: On `S`, terminate with integer exit status `C` from 0 through 255.

primitives.name: ABORT
primitives.description: Abandon the current top-level run.

primitives.name: BREAKPOINT
primitives.description: Pause the program here and return to the prompt, which then runs at this point until `STEP`, `NEXT`, `CONTINUE` or `STOP`. It does nothing where the program cannot be paused: in a script or an included file, in a nested run such as `PARALLEL`, and in hosts without a prompt.

primitives.name: STEP
primitives.description: Resume the paused program and pause again before the next word it calls, also inside the definitions it calls. Raises `Debug-Error` if no program is paused.

primitives.name: NEXT
primitives.description: Resume the paused program and pause again before the next word at the same depth or shallower, running the definitions it calls without pausing. Raises `Debug-Error` if no program is paused.

primitives.name: CONTINUE
primitives.description: Resume the paused program until the next `BREAKPOINT` or its end. Raises `Debug-Error` if no program is paused.

primitives.name: STOP
primitives.description: Drop the paused program without running the rest of it, keeping the stacks. Raises `Debug-Error` if no program is paused.

primitives.name: BACKTRACE
primitives.description: On `S`, push the list `L` of the programs being run, innermost first. Each is a list `(NAME PROGRAM INDEX)`: `NAME` is a unit with the word whose call started it (`()` if none did), `PROGRAM` is the list it runs and `INDEX` the number of its elements that have already run.

primitives.name: UNITTYPE
primitives.description: On `S`, inspect the element type of unit `U`: 0 number, 1 list, or 2 word.

primitives.name: WORD
primitives.description: On `S`, convert valid word-name text `T` to a word unit.

primitives.name: TEXT
primitives.description: On `S`, convert word unit `U` to its name as text.
